# uem_application_assignment (Resource)

Manages a Workspace ONE UEM Application Assignment

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "application_uuid" {
  type        = string
  description = "UUID of the application to manage assignment rules for"
}

variable "smart_group_uuid" {
  type        = string
  description = "Smart group UUID to assign the application to"
}

resource "uem_application_assignment" "example" {
  application_uuid = var.application_uuid

  excluded_smart_groups = []

  assignments = [
    {
      priority = 0

      distribution = {
        name                = "All users"
        description         = "Terraform-managed assignment"
        smart_groups        = [var.smart_group_uuid]
        app_delivery_method = "AUTO"
      }

      restriction = {
        remove_on_unenroll = true
      }
    },
  ]
}

output "application_assignment_id" {
  description = "Assignment resource ID (mirrors application_uuid)"
  value       = uem_application_assignment.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `application_uuid` (String) UUID of the application this assignment rule applies to. Changing this targets a different application's assignment rule (the UEM assignment API is scoped per application UUID) rather than updating the current one in place, so it forces replacement — otherwise `id` (which mirrors application_uuid) would change across what Terraform planned as an in-place update, which the framework rejects as an inconsistent provider result.

### Optional

- `assignments` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--assignments))
- `excluded_smart_groups` (List of String) Omitting it from configuration resets it to `[]` on apply: UEM's
  assignment-rules update is a full replace, and an omitted field is not kept.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--assignments"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignments`

Required:

- `distribution` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--assignments--distribution))
- `priority` (Number) The priorities of the n assignments must be exactly 0 to n-1, with no gaps or duplicates: UEM
  itself rejects anything else. Separately, `terraform plan` also requires the assignments to be listed in ascending
  priority order (0 first) — this ordering requirement is a provider-side limitation (UEM's own API accepts an
  out-of-order list), not a UEM rule.

Optional:

- `restriction` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--assignments--restriction))

<a id="nestedatt--assignments--distribution"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignments.distribution`

Required:

- `name` (String)
- `smart_groups` (List of String) The provider lowercases the configured UUIDs for stable diffs.

Optional:

- `app_delivery_method` (String) Omitting it from configuration resets it to `ON_DEMAND` on apply: UEM's
  assignment-rules update is a full replace, and an omitted field is not kept.
- `description` (String)
- `effective_date` (String) RFC3339 effective date. When unset at create, UEM stamps the current date; an import captures the date UEM has. Set it explicitly to pin it. Removing it from the configuration lets UEM re-stamp it at the next apply.


<a id="nestedatt--assignments--restriction"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignments.restriction`

Optional:

- `remove_on_unenroll` (Boolean)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
#!/bin/bash
# Import an existing Workspace ONE application assignment rule into Terraform

# Import by application UUID
# Usage: terraform import uem_application_assignment.example "<application_uuid>"

terraform import uem_application_assignment.example "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
```
